subject: Fear of the cockroach
alt: Cartoon: two pairs of frightened eyes peer from behind a dark window. One says: shut the trains, shut the buses, shut the planes, shut the metro, shut the internet, deploy the police, deploy the CRPF, RAF, CISF, BSF, ITBP, RSS, Bajrang Dal, ABC, BCD, deploy everyone. The other asks: should we deploy nuclear bombs as well? Outside, a tiny cockroach sits on the wall.
chutki: The smallest character in the whole cartoon is a cockroach sitting on the wall, and the biggest fear is of it. The eyes peering from behind the window are so shaken that they draw up a list of shutting trains, buses, metro and internet and deploying every uniform and every squad. The list is so long that in the end it reaches ABC and BCD, because in panic even the letters start to look like weapons.

Dhodapkar's satire lies in this proportion: on one side the entire might of power, on the other a tiny creature that is just sitting on the wall. The young people who were jokingly called cockroaches know that a cockroach does not end by being crushed. And when someone asks whether to deploy nuclear bombs too, it is clear that those who look for a cure for fear in weapons end up shutting their own window.
